walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Presentation & Interpretation — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Presentation & Interpretation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Presentation & Interpretation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: If you divide both sides of an inequality by -2, what happens to the inequality sign?
options: 4.65, because rounding to 1 dp means cutting after the second decimal.
The inequality sign reverses (e.g. > becomes <).
The inequality becomes an equals sign.
The inequality sign stays the same — you treat it like an equation.
4.65, because rounding to 1 dp means cutting after the second decimal.
4.6 — look at the second decimal (4), which is less than 5, so round down.
4.7, because the 8 at the end rounds the 4 up to 5, which then rounds the 6 up to 7.
The inequality becomes an equals sign.

mcqs.q: Can a probability ever be greater than 1?
options: Yes — if an event is very likely, the probability can be 1.5 or 2.
No — probabilities range from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
Yes, but only when expressed as a percentage.
4.65, because rounding to 1 dp means cutting after the second decimal.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sampling”?
options: Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.
Mean = sum/n. Median = middle value of ordered data. Mode = most frequent value. Different averages, different uses.
Random, stratified, systematic, opportunity, quota. Aim: representative of population without bias.
Show min, Q₁, median, Q₃, max. Visualise spread, skew, outliers. Useful for comparing distributions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Range, IQR, SD”?
options: Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.
Random, stratified, systematic, opportunity, quota. Aim: representative of population without bias.
Range = max − min. IQR = Q₃ − Q₁ (middle 50% spread). Standard deviation σ = √(variance), more sensitive measure.
Running total. Plotting against upper class boundary gives an S-curve, used to estimate medians and quartiles.
